title: Bioinformatics and Network Analysis of Microarray Data from Mixture Cell Type
author: Evan Maestri
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.btqfnmtn
materials: Option 2: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA). IPA is a commercial software package. QIAGEN Knowledge Base aids in the biological contexts of expression analysis experiments. Generate enriched canonical pathways, drug targets in networks, and disease-associations of your expression data. IPA will identify significant pathways (indicate activation/inhibition prediction) and discover regulatory networks. The User Manual and IPA-Data-Analysis-training-slides.pdf provide protocols for proper data entry and best practices for network generation. Run a new core expression analysis in IPA. This will assess signaling pathways, regulators, molecular interaction networks, and disease and biological functions modulated based on expression changes in the input dataset. Upload data (gene expression, protein expression, metabolomics). Select core analysis settings. Specify the reference set (e.g. Mouse Gene 1.0 ST Array). Select network relationship type (direct and indirect or only direct). Set data cutoff filters by fold-change and p-value. Fischer’s exact test in IPA will determine enriched canonical pathways for each gene subset entered. Select individual canonical pathways of interest to be overlapped and displayed as a network. For example, in an immune-system dataset B-cell, T-cell, NK-cell pathway annotations can be overlapped to identify major regulators. In cancer contexts, canonical pathways regulating epithelial neoplasms, abdominal carcinomas, digestive organ tumors, apoptosis, and proliferative pathways may yield predictive drug targets and novel regulators. Overlaps between gene subsets in enriched canonical pathways can be selected and displayed as a network. Overlaying an analysis can color the genes by their up or down regulation (color intensity by fold change). See the user manual for overlaying datasets, analyses, and lists . Ingenuity Pathway Analysis QIAGEN Causal analysis approaches in Ingenuity Pathway Analysis.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England).

steps.title: Conduct Tissue-Associated Protein Enrichment Analysis
steps.instruction: Use DAVID Bioinformatics 6.8 and its Functional Annotation Tool with the Uniprot tissue (UP_tissue) annotation database to generate tissue-specific gene subsets.

substeps.instruction: Upload the query gene list of interest.
Select the accession identifier (e.g., Ensembl, Refseq, Genbank) and specify the appropriate genetic background.
Within the annotation summary of results, select 'Tissue_Expression'.
Display the chart for the Up_tissue annotations.

Download the gene list per selected tissue of interest (e.g., for immune system genes, select jejunal and colic lymph nodes, spleen, activated spleen, and thymus; for epithelial genes, select colon, liver, kidney, and small intestine).

steps.title: Perform Gene Ontology (GO) Analysis
steps.instruction: Identify enriched or over-represented annotations within gene sets using GO analysis.

substeps.instruction: Run GO analysis on the entire list of genes in the dataset.
Separate expression data into smaller subsets (e.g., upregulated genes and downregulated genes).
Run GO analysis on both subsets to identify tissue-specific pathways.

steps.title: Perform Alternative Enrichment Analysis
steps.instruction: Utilize STRING or PANTHER as alternative tools for protein/gene classification and enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Option 1 (STRING v.11): Submit a query of proteins to determine enriched annotations in the network compared to background; color the graph by selecting functional enrichments in GO terms.

Option 2 (PANTHER v.16.0): Enter IDs for gene list analysis (mouse or human), select analysis type (functional classification, statistical overrepresentation testing, or statistical enrichment testing), and toggle between Ontology classifications (molecular function, biological process, cellular component, protein class, and pathway) to identify hits and gene lists.

steps.title: Perform Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
steps.instruction: Execute GSEA or GSEA Preranked to interpret genome-wide expression profiles.

substeps.instruction: Create an expression dataset .txt file containing genes/probes and expression values for each feature.
For GSEA Preranked, supply a list of genes ranked by p-value and direction of fold change.
Obtain a gene set file (gmx or gmt format) from BaderLab for human, mouse, or rat (e.g., GO Biological Processes, All Pathways, Drug Targets, and Disease Phenotypes).
To improve evidence codes, select files with 'no GO iea' to exclude IEA, ND, and RCA codes.
Run GSEA using default settings, ensuring 'collapse dataset to gene symbols' is set to 'false'.

steps.title: Visualize Gene Sets via Enrichment Map
steps.instruction: Use the EnrichmentMap app in Cytoscape v3.8.2 to visualize gene-set enrichment as a network.

substeps.instruction: Generate enrichments outside of EnrichmentMap.
Import results into EnrichmentMap, selecting significant gene sets based on specified p-value and FDR cutoffs.

steps.title: Generate Protein-Protein Interaction Networks
steps.instruction: Create networks for individual gene subsets (e.g., immune vs epithelial) to identify key hubs and regulators.

substeps.instruction: Using STRING v11: Search by single protein name, multiple proteins, or amino acid sequence and specify the organism.
Configure active interaction sources (fusion, neighborhood, cooccurrence, experimental, textmining, database, and coexpression).
Select 'experimental' evidence with high (0.7) or highest (0.9) confidence for best reliability.
Hide disconnected nodes and download the network as a static png or scalable vector graphic.

steps.title: Analyze Networks in Cytoscape
steps.instruction: Import STRING or IPA networks into Cytoscape for advanced visualization and statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Install the stringApp to import STRING networks.
Perform protein, PubMed, disease, or protein/compound queries.
Identify GO, KEGG Pathways, and protein domain enrichments at specific significance levels.
Use the network analyzer tool to calculate directed analysis statistics: number of proteins, edges, average number of neighbors, clustering coefficient, and network density.
Identify major network regulators by selecting those with the greatest edge connectivity (highest input/output connections).
Remove unconnected nodes for improved visualization.

steps.title: Conduct Transcription Factor and Co-occurrence Analysis
steps.instruction: Use ChEA3 and Enrichr to identify regulatory elements and gene signatures.

substeps.instruction: ChEA3: Input a list of human or mouse gene symbols to identify associated transcription factors (TFs).
Enrichr: Submit a list of Entrez gene symbols or BED format files to determine co-occurrence with other genes or signatures from single TF perturbations.

steps.title: Perform Specialized Immune-System Analysis
steps.instruction: Utilize Interferome and ImmGen resources for deeper decomposition of cellular mixtures.

substeps.instruction: Interferome v.2: Search by Gene Symbol, GenBank Accession, or Ensembl ID. Specify treatment concentration, time, in vivo/in vitro status, organ, cell-type, cell line, and fold change. Use 'TF Analysis' to generate a figure of the promoter region (-1500 to 500 bp) with predicted TF-binding elements.

ImmGen: Use DataBrowsers for mouse immune cell expression. Use the Single Cell Portal for RNA-seq profiles, Gene Skyline for gene visualization across populations (B cells, T cells, macrophages), and Gene Constellation for correlated gene graphics. Toggle between STRING and Enrichr tabs from the input gene.

description: Option 1: DAVID Bioinformatics. From the annotation summary results of your input gene list entered in go to step #2 , select the category Gene_Ontology. By default, biological process, cellular component, and molecular function will be selected.
